prompt: an engine builder about restoring a coral reef: buy coral and fish cards from a shared current, corals feed the fish living on them every season, and three public reef goals reward different strategies
rival observatories fund telescopes that collect starlight each night, spend it to publish discoveries for points, and race to claim three research milestones before anyone else

a steampunk workshop where you craft gears and copper into machines that upgrade what your workshop produces; every third round an exhibition pays the player with the most machines of the featured type
a deck-building game about wandering musicians: start with a deck of simple tunes, buy better songs from a market row, and perform concerts in towns that pay off for particular styles

a worker placement game in a mountain monastery: send monks to the scriptorium, vineyard and market to make manuscripts and wine, and win a bonus each season for having the most monks in the chapter house
harbor captains send crew to the docks, warehouses and guild hall to load ships, then sail cargo to three colonies where majorities score after each of three voyages
rival clans spread influence across five valleys of a mountain kingdom; each round one valley holds a festival that scores its majority, and spending favor lets a clan move influence between valleys
a city politics game where factions send delegates to six districts; the strongest faction in a district uses its special power, and three elections score district control
settle a chain of volcanic islands: build lodges on hex corners and trails along the edges, an eruption deck decides which terrain produces, and players trade obsidian, timber and fish to grow
rival rail barons lay track along hex edges between mining towns, deliver ore and coal to cities for points, and trade with each other for the goods they are missing
colonize Mars: build domes on crater rims and pipelines between them; ice and regolith tiles produce every sol, and shipping goods back to Earth is costly but scores big
a two-player duel over a river delta: build mills and canals, harvest grain and clay, and trade with a bank whose prices shift with every trade
build a shared walled city from square tiles: streets, markets and walls must match at the edges, and a district closed off by walls scores for whoever has the most guildhalls inside it
grow a coral archipelago from hex tiles with sea, reef and sand edges; when an island is completed it scores for the player with the most villages on it
plant a shared botanical garden from hex tiles whose flowerbeds must touch matching colors; every player also holds secret goals about which colors they want the largest beds of
draw a city's subway map from square tiles whose edges carry colored lines; long unbroken lines through your stations score, and dead ends can cut off a rival's line

plan a night market by drafting: pick one stall card from your hand and pass the rest, over three rounds that alternate direction; food stalls, lanterns and musicians each score sets in a different way
draft spells over three ages and inscribe them into your grimoire; spells cost mana that earlier spells produce, and combos between schools of magic score at the end
collect exotic birds from a face-up row of cards; spend matching cards to complete flocks for points, and the first player to complete each kind of flock earns a bonus
a deck builder about a spice company: buy ships and merchants into your deck, send ships on voyages that pay out when you play the right cards together, and trash your starting coins to thin the deck
a hidden-role game for 5 to 8 players: a council of mages votes on which rituals to perform, but two of them are secretly cultists who win if three corrupted rituals pass
sealed bids for ancient relics: each round everyone secretly bids a numbered card from their hand, the highest bid takes the relic, and collections of relics score as sets
a cooperative game on a flooding deep-sea station: each round event cards flood rooms, and the crew must pump out water and repair all four reactors before the station sinks
prospectors secretly send miners to gold claims at the same time, then reveal; the biggest crew at each claim takes its gold, and bluffing about where you are going is half the game
